topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation and outlines how previously introduced immune components will be examined in depth.

topics.label: Innate Recognition of Pathogens and Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the molecular basis of innate immune sensing, including the characteristics of PAMPs and DAMPs and the functions of pattern recognition receptor families such as TLRs and inflammasomes.

topics.label: Cellular Activation, Leukocyte Recruitment, and Systemic Effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells direct the physical recruitment of circulating leukocytes into tissues, facilitate lymphatic drainage, and potentially trigger systemic complications like septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the active and passive mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, mediate tissue repair and scarring, and lead to persistent adaptations such as granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks for the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the complement system.
